evidence.quote: The majority of the lake is within the United States, but two bays along the north shore extend over the international border into Canada.

evidence.claim: The 1,544-acre lake occupies part of the Turtle Mountains and reaches a maximum depth of 24 feet.
evidence.quote: Lake Metigoshe is a 1,544-acre (625 ha) lake in both Bottineau County, North Dakota and the Rural Municipality of Winchester, Manitoba.  It is located in the Turtle Mountains on the Canada–United States border and has a maximum depth of 24 feet (7.3 m).

evidence.claim: White settlers called it Fish Lake, a name recorded on an early plat map of Roland Township.
evidence.quote: When the lake was first discovered by white settlers, it was called Fish Lake, and this name appears on an early plat map of Roland Township.

evidence.claim: That older map name remains attached to Little Fish Lake, a bay connected to the Canadian part of the lake.
evidence.quote: The original name lives on in one of the bays attached to the Canadian portion of the lake (Little Fish Lake).

evidence.claim: The International Peace Garden straddles the Manitoba–North Dakota boundary, a park established on July 14, 1932, to symbolize peaceful relations between Canada and the United States.
evidence.quote: The International Peace Garden (French: Jardin international de la paix) is a 9.5-square-kilometre (3.7 sq mi) park located adjacent to the International Peace Garden Border Crossing along the Canada–United States border between the province of Manitoba and the state of North Dakota.  It was established on July 14, 1932, as a symbol of the peaceful relationship between the two countries.

evidence.claim: It gave North Dakota its Peace Garden State nickname, which appeared on vehicle plates in 1956 and became official the following year.
evidence.quote: The slogan Peace Garden State originates from the International Peace Garden, and was added to vehicle registration plates of North Dakota  in 1956, In the next year, the North Dakota Legislative Assembly made the slogan an official state nickname.

evidence.claim: An 18-foot floral clock and fountains are among the garden’s features.
evidence.quote: Main features of the garden include an 5.5-metre (18 ft) floral clock display, and fountains.

evidence.claim: The twin concrete peace towers were demolished in 2017 after weather-related erosion made them unsafe.
evidence.quote: the concrete towers had been declared unsafe due to irreparable weather-related erosion and were demolished in 2017.

evidence.claim: All visitors must pass through their destination country’s immigration procedures when leaving the garden, including those returning to the country they entered from.
evidence.quote: requiring all visitors – including those returning to the country from which they arrived – to go through the immigration procedures of their destination country upon leaving the garden.

evidence.claim: The site also offers a panoramic view across the Turtle Mountains and the surrounding valley, alongside its astronomical instruments.
evidence.quote: A panoramic view of the Turtle Mountains, as well as the surrounding valley, is available from the site.

evidence.claim: Lake Metigoshe State Park encompasses about a quarter of the shoreline, along the east half of the portion known locally as North Lake.
evidence.quote: The Lake Metigoshe State Park encompasses about of a quarter of the lake's overall shoreline (or the east half of what is locally known as 'North Lake').

evidence.claim: The garden’s fourteen Arma Sifton bells were a 1972 gift from Central United Church in Brandon, Manitoba.
evidence.quote: The Arma Sifton bells are a chime of 14 bells cast by Gillett & Johnston bellfounders. The bells were a gift from Central United Church of Brandon, Manitoba in 1972.
